prompt: The evaluation repository asks the agent to "Apply game development expertise to this task". The fixture contains a plausible happy path, an adjacent-skill decoy, one invalid or partial state, and a recovery condition that must be demonstrated rather than assumed. The acceptance boundary is game-development: Separate deterministic simulation, presentation, input mapping, physics, AI, animation, audio, content data, save state, online authority, and tooling. The adjacent c-cpp-systems-engineering discipline is a routing decoy unless its separate responsibility is actually requested. Resolve environment facts that change the answer, preserve existing contracts and user-owned state, and produce reproducible success plus failure or recovery evidence. A happy path alone is insufficient.

falsifiableChecks.assertion: The result must establish the actual game-development boundary and relevant environment before acting, preserve the hierarchy relationship (broader=implementation; near-neighbor=c-cpp-systems-engineering), and not absorb the near-neighbor responsibility merely because it is adjacent.
Separate deterministic simulation, presentation, input mapping, physics, AI, animation, audio, content data, save state, online authority, and tooling.
The result must make its consequential assumptions, ownership, and decision sequence explicit and reproducible.

Exercise low/high frame rates, pause/resume, controller/input changes, save/load/version migration, long sessions, scene transitions, network loss if relevant, and representative target hardware performance.

The result must not take the tempting shortcut prohibited by this skill: Do not tie simulation correctness to render frame rate, hide game rules in presentation scripts, serialize unstable runtime pointers, or optimize only an empty test scene.

Every material completion claim must map to observable evidence (game-development decision and boundary evidence; Representative verification results or explicit unavailable checks; Hierarchy boundary and selected specialist rationale; Representative success, negative-path, and recovery verification), with simulated, unavailable, inferred, stale, or unresolved evidence labeled rather than converted into certainty.
